title: Endpoint SLI Signature and Degradation Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define a compact, machine-readable SLI signature for all user-facing endpoints and model variants, and publish an operational playbook for graduated degradation (degradable slices) during regional capacity pressure. This ticket specifies per-endpoint SLIs (latency quantiles, availability, correctness proxy), the error-budget enforcement ladder (soft evict -> variant downgrade -> circuit-breaker -> shed to cache), and the multi-region failover weighting rules that preserve error budget for high-priority slices. Objective: provide deterministic, auditable behavior for the Console and API teams when capacity constraints or infra incidents occur.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLI signature document exists and is consumable by the telemetry pipeline (fields: endpoint_id, model_id, variant, p50/p95/p99 latency, availability, correctness_rate, rollout_slice)
Degradation playbook defines at least 4 ordered enforcement steps with concrete thresholds and automated actions for each step
Circuit breaker and load-shedding thresholds are expressed in terms of 5m burn rate and absolute concurrent in-flight limits and are configurable per-route via Console
A staged rollout plan and chaos-testing checklist are documented, with a Grafana dashboard and alerting rules for burn-rate and slice eviction events
Runbooks updated with the playbook and validated by on-call SRE during a tabletop exercise
tasks: Draft SLI signature spec and JSON schema for ingestion into telemetry service
Map existing routes and model variants to SLI signatures (automated script + manual review)
Define tiered enforcement ladder with numeric thresholds for P50/P95/P99 and error budget burn rates
Implement circuit-breaker config knobs in routing layer and expose via Console feature flag
Create synthetic tests to validate downgrade and cache-shed behaviors under load
Create Grafana dashboards + alerts and tie to PagerDuty runbook steps
Coordinate with Product for per-customer SLA overrides and with Sales/Success for affected customers
comments: 2026-02-12 - Ava Chen: Initial draft uploaded. Focused on making SLIs model-aware (token-level correctness proxy for gen routes). Asked for ENG/Telemetry review.
2026-02-18 - Priya Nair (Telemetry): Reviewed JSON schema, suggested adding 'rollout_slice' and 'snapshot_window' fields. Flagged ingestion rate impact for high-cardinality variant tags.

2026-02-25 - Diego Morales: Proposed enforcement ladder: (1) soft-evict low-priority slices, (2) model-variant downgrade to quantized/faster variant, (3) route-level circuit-breaker with 30s TTL, (4) short-circuit to cached or canned response. Seeking PM sign-off on customer-visible degradations.
2026-03-03 - Marcus Li (Product): Approved the ladder in principle but requested a visible Console banner and telemetry labeling for any customer experiencing degradations.
2026-03-06 - Security review: Security team confirmed no additional data controls required for this policy; private deployments must opt into auto-eviction behavior (per legal/enterprise request).
2026-03-10 - QA: Added stress test scenarios that reproduce soft-eviction and verify request-level headers contain 'x-redwood-degraded: true' when serving degraded responses.
decision_log: Dec 1: Use p50/p95/p99 latency quantiles + availability(HTTP 2xx fraction) + a domain-specific correctness proxy as the canonical SLI trio for generative routes.
Dec 8: Prefer model-variant downgrade (e.g., move from float16 to int8 quantized variant) over wholesale route drop to preserve availability while controlling cost.
Feb 25: Adopt a 5-minute rolling burn-rate window for error-budget enforcement; require 3 consecutive windows breaching threshold before escalating enforcement level.
Mar 3: Multi-region failover should respect slice reservations: high-priority slices retain 20% reserved capacity in failover region to avoid cold-start degradation for premium customers.
